title: Language Model Fine-Tuning on Scaled Survey Data for Predicting Distributions of Public Opinions
findings: Fine-tuning on the SubPOP dataset significantly improved the models' ability to predict the opinion distributions of diverse religious groups. The Wasserstein Distance (a measure of error) was consistently reduced across all tested religious groups (Protestant, Jewish, Hindu, Atheist, Muslim) for all models after fine-tuning. For example, in the OpinionQA evaluation, the fine-tuned Llama-3-70B model reduced the error for the Protestant group from a baseline of 0.143 to 0.086 and for the Muslim group from 0.202 to 0.159, demonstrating a more accurate reflection of these groups' survey responses.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the accuracy of Large Language Models in predicting the distribution of public opinions for various subpopulations, including specific religious groups. The evaluation metric was the Wasserstein distance (WD) between the model's predicted distribution of survey responses and the actual distribution from human respondents within each religious group.
